category_notes.text: Invoke's current primary site was inspected for its image-creation workflow; today's image clients and ComfyUI integrations require their own full code grants and separate model/provider review.

OpenReelio now has a complete MIT code-grant review and a detailed guide here. Its0.1.x agent/QC limits, optional transcription build, unsigned installers and future video-generation roadmap are distinguished from implemented editing.

OpenSuno's current music-generation site was inspected; software, YuE2/checkpoint terms and generated-output rights remain separate. Today's audio guides distinguish local compute from hosted services.
SolidCraft's primary site documents an AI-assisted 3D/CAD workflow. The site is a discovery source; dimensional correctness and physical print fitness are not inferred.
The WebLLM primary paper supplies browser-local inference context, not a blanket compatibility pass for creative web apps or all WebGPU devices.
Meta's primary Immersive Web SDK/AI development article was inspected. AI-assisted authoring, headset runtime support and required proprietary hosts are distinct questions.
Fragment's shader/computational-art site was inspected. A useful conventional art framework is not admitted as an AI tool without a concrete AI integration.
ossia's primary interactive-installation documentation informs control and installation workflows; it does not by itself clear a new AI application or its complete grant.

SOMA now has a detailed guide and complete GPL/Model Exception review. It explicitly remains an early prototype; agent-authored geometry and STL/STEP export do not establish physical fabrication fitness.
ForgeAX's own authoring documentation supplements game-tool discovery. Finished games and tools merely written with AI were screened separately from implemented creator AI workflows.

Movens-Zero primary documentation was inspected but no complete root software grant was recovered. EDGE is preserved as a MIT-screened music-to-dance lead with model/data/rig and historical setup limits.
The AVTR-1 model card was inspected for talking-character research. Exact checkpoint, code, identity/voice assets and deployment rights need separate clearance.
The primary Light-Aware Compositing paper was inspected as neural compositing research. A paper/demo does not clear redistributed models or prove production compositing fidelity.
A live Neural Acoustic Fields for Mixed Reality PDF attempt was bounded at2MB. The incomplete paper capture is an explicit evidence limit, not a complete spatial-audio review.
Primary volumetric-capture research supplements camera/reconstruction discovery; code/checkpoint access and useful creator output still require project-specific checks.
Current Subtitle Edit documentation was inspected for AI-assisted transcription/localization workflows. A mature host does not clear every optional model, API or platform path.
SVGRender's official model/source context was inspected. Editable vector output, fonts and model permissions must be checked independently of rendered previews.
The primary VecGlypher paper was inspected for learned glyph/vector creation. Typeface rights, usable font export and platform requirements remain unresolved for new feature admission.
Dramai's primary project page returned a thin script/navigation shell. It is retained as a discovery attempt, not usable implementation or quality evidence.

OpenSlides' official site failed TLS. The weekly review separately recovered current GitLab README, complete alternative MIT/Apache grants and dependency notes; optional MCP still needs an unpublished crate.
The primary Autochrome-related paper was inspected for computational photo workflows; generic paper results are not a pass for an unspecified camera/device or checkpoint.
A primary deep-learning scientific-visualization survey was inspected to widen adjacent discovery; a survey is a source of leads, not itself an eligible creator application.
MIT Media Lab Illuminate's project overview was inspected. No new implemented AI role/full software grant was cleared from that overview alone.
ossia's projection-mapping documentation supplies performance-host context. Mapping capability alone does not establish AI functionality or venue-ready operation.

OpenTryOn current source explicitly applies CC BY-NC 4.0to software. Despite its open-source wording, it is excluded from the eligible library; model catalog breadth is not license or quality clearance.
W3C's primary audio-description guidance informs what creator accessibility tools should deliver. The guidance is not an AI software tool or a claim of automated compliance.
Google's official Android MediaPipe segmentation guide supplements on-device media discovery. API documentation does not establish the complete app's device matrix or privacy behavior.

KinoDraw now has a full guide: local neural voice and doodle search, optional AI direction, editable explainer videos and explicit model/asset terms. Its original MIT source and GPL-packaged apps are distinguished.
PyPottery's primary project site was inspected for digitization/analysis context; model, archaeological-data and software rights need independent distinction.
MAESTRO's primary project was inspected for emerging choreography/motion authoring. Research provenance alone neither promotes quality nor assigns Experimental.
The primary TouchTwin-related paper was inspected for AI/touch interaction. Physical output/device validation and full grants remain unresolved before feature admission.

NeRAF current code is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0and is excluded from eligible software. AudioStellar current sources were reviewed separately; that musical sampler and scene-acoustic inference are distinct scopes.
OpenMagia's primary site and the OpenSlides TLS attempt were inspected. Agent connection instructions without implemented tools were held; separately paid services stay labeled.
LyriFont primary project material was inspected but no complete current root software grant was recovered; it remains a local/watchlist lead rather than an eligible tool.

MAESTRO primary project material was inspected, but its complete root software grant was not recovered. EDGE supplies an additional MIT-screened editable dance-motion lead; owner research results do not establish independent use.
Ink Blossom's primary project page was inspected for algorithmic/AI craft interfaces. No physical crafting guarantee or new complete software grant was established from the page alone.
Tmd-TS and perso-ai primary sources supplement score discovery. Today's ComposerLint guide distinguishes analysis, bounded edits, patched rendering and human-approved exports.
Aegir's primary site was inspected for learned lighting/light-field context. Demo images do not establish exact material, view-consistency or checkpoint permissions.
The primary AromaGen paper was inspected to extend discovery into scent-related creative interfaces. It does not establish a deployable, licensed physical scent system.
AgenticCAD current code is PolyForm Noncommercial and is excluded. SOMA and the other reviewed CAD/architecture tools are concept/design workflows, not certified construction or engineering approval.
Aegir's primary project context was inspected; capture/display hardware and model-specific terms remain distinct from web previews.
A primary learned-puppetry/character-control paper was inspected. No universal rig compatibility or production retargeting pass was established.
PyPotteryTrace's official documentation was inspected for learned tracing/ceramic analysis. A tracing demo is not physical fabrication validation.
The SOMA full guide separates GPL source and the model-output exception; its prototype/API limits remain visible. AgenticCAD is excluded because its software grant is noncommercial.
The primary MapStory PDF capture was bounded at2MB. Map/story generation remains a lead; complete methods, code/license and geographic accuracy are not established by the partial capture.

FORM is a MIT-screened developer building block for identified material-shaping simulations and rendered interaction studies; that creative application is an explicit inference from its shaping/presentation exports. Reproduction data are not publicly hosted and physical execution remains unverified.
OpenToonz's official site supplies conventional animation-host context. No new AI tool was admitted merely because this animation host is open source.
FolAI's primary project page was inspected for generated audio effects. Exact checkpoint/output terms and listening evidence remain separate from demonstration clips.
A primary neural codec paper was inspected. Rate/distortion claims, runtime implementation, bitstream compatibility and model terms require scoped verification.
Sonify's Parallax primary page was inspected for AI/data-art practice. A commissioned artwork or service page is not proof of an open-source reusable tool.

Brain2Music's primary research page broadens neural-signal creative discovery. Today's NeuroCanvas guide documents EEG controls while disclosing weak estimates and unresolved dataset-derived model rights.
VideoNeuMat current original code uses CC BY-NC 4.0; Apache licensing of some third-party components does not clear its own software. It is excluded from eligible results.
The primary Neural Cameras paper capture was bounded at2MB. Camera conditioning remains research context; full methods and deployable grant review are incomplete.
A primary paper-engineering research page was inspected for emerging AI/craft connections. No new complete licensed implementation or physical build result was established.
OpenCAD Irrigation and LibreTerrain primary sources were inspected. Current terrain/agent tools are distinct from irrigation engineering or site approval.
Visual Anagrams' primary page was inspected for learned multi-view/perceptual image design. Model and source-grant checks remain separate from optical examples.
Visual Anagrams' primary project supplements perceptual-image discovery. A compelling illusion does not establish general creative output reliability.
Imprimatur's primary site was inspected for print/engraving context. No concrete new AI function/full software grant was cleared from that conventional workflow page alone.
A primary learned-brushstroke paper was inspected. Stylized output, editable strokes and physical brush execution need separate evidence.
HueForge's primary documentation was inspected for color/palette work. Product licensing and actual AI contribution require project-specific checks before new admission.
The Library of Congress Collaging Space-Time project was inspected for computational archive/collage practice. Collection access does not clear every asset or establish a reusable AI application.
Primary deep-stereo research was inspected. Single-image examples do not validate headset comfort, calibrated depth or every stereo conversion workflow.

The Semantic Gaussians URL returned a redirect/placeholder response rather than substantive current implementation documentation. No complete new source/license review was established from that capture.
PHOSA's primary project was inspected for sign/avatar media context. Linguistic accuracy, signer representation and animation/model permissions remain unresolved.

The NAM Web Player announcement and Embedded Amp Model README were inspected. The latter's current tests use synthetic targets; MCU estimates and C/PyTorch agreement are not a physical pedal/audio-quality pass.
World Shaper's primary site was inspected for generative environment workflows. Navigable previews do not establish geometry consistency or deployment rights.
The virtual-try-on animation source has a custom noncommercial scientific/education/art grant, so it is excluded as open-source software. Clothing-fit or model rights are not inferred.
X-Dub's primary project was inspected for speech/video localization. Today's subtitles, narration and talking-avatar entries retain model/service terms and manual review limits.
Reshoot Anything's official model documentation was inspected. Camera/identity preservation and exact model terms need scoped review before production claims.

Intel Open Image Denoise now has a detailed guide and full Apache-2.0 grant comparison. CPU/multivendor GPU requirements, rendererAOVs, example CLI format limits and unverified scene/temporal quality are separated.

A primary media-evaluation paper and TensorStack's NuGet version index were inspected. Registry presence is not an independent perceptual-quality benchmark; today's takecheck lead still needs a detailed guide.
Imprimatur's primary page was inspected; it does not establish AI-assisted prepress, color-managed output, bleed or production printing readiness.
AlayaWorld current root LTX 2 Community grant includes use/revenue conditions covering code and weights. It stays in the restricted-code watchlist, not the eligible open-source library.
A primary neural audio/control paper was inspected for learned patching practice. No new full software/dependency review was completed from the paper alone.
The Optica primary-paper route returned an access/login response rather than usable complete paper text. No alternate route bypassed it; the method and code/license review remain gaps.
A primary immersive/dome media paper was inspected. Dome projection geometry, venue calibration and audience-ready playback are not inferred.
StitchFoundry's primary site was inspected for AI/craft discovery. Stitch-file export is distinct from successful machine stitching, fabric behavior and licensed model use.
Imprimatur supplies adjacent print practice context. Conventional print utilities remain outside the eligible AI library without a specific implemented AI role.
Nasjonalmuseet's local-AI semantic-search article, ZKM code context and LinkedCulture's primary description were inspected. Collection/data rights and reusable source grants remain separate.
Eagle Animation's site returned a thin JavaScript shell; no new implemented AI contribution/full software grant was cleared from that capture.
A primary soundscape/ecology paper was inspected for adjacent AI listening practice. Scientific sound classification does not automatically establish a creative authoring tool.
Primary anamorphic-image research was inspected. View-dependent examples are not a physical installation or manufacturing pass.
The primary light-field neural-rendering project was inspected. Device/viewing-zone support and visual comfort remain unresolved for practical display use.
A primary astronomical AI imaging paper was inspected. Scientific validity and aesthetic media generation are distinct; no absent instrument requirements were inferred.
Primary tactile-graphics research was inspected for accessible creative output. Embossing/printing success and tactile readability require physical/user evidence.
UDnet's primary project was inspected for learned underwater imagery. Water/color recovery claims do not establish scientific color fidelity or every camera's support.
The primary EUSIPCO paper was inspected for acoustic-field synthesis. Transducer/controller hardware, execution and physical field quality remain unverified.
CalliRewrite's primary project was inspected. Brush/robot compatibility and actual calligraphic results require evidence beyond a demo page.
Comictl's primary documentation and current manga projects were inspected. Today's localization leads separate OCR, neural translation, inpainting, editable typesetting and rights to source pages.
Shopprentice's primary site and current carpentry/CAD repositories were inspected. Tool-head tracking and agent-designed geometry do not certify workshop safety or physical tolerances.

Taarib's primary documentation and current multilingual localization sources were inspected. Today's game-localization entries retain original-game rights, placeholder checks and model/service limits.
LacyLights' primary site was inspected. Today's StageMind/followspot leads have concrete AI roles, but physical fixtures, tracking performance and venue safety remain unverified.

The primary Music2P paper is about music-conditioned album-cover images, not photobook layout; it does not satisfy the layout field. Today's Photo Organiser AI guide supplies an actual photobook planning/page-preview workflow, with print-ready export unverified.

WAIve Pulse's primary site was inspected, but its complete code grant adds Commons Clause NoSell and is excluded. Today's local audio guides distinguish generated loops/one-shots from model-specific rights and audition requirements.

ecosystem_checks.finding: Current full-source attempts for AudioStellar, perso-ai, LibreTerrain, EmbeddedAmp, OpenDub and OpenSlides were reviewed in the weekly pass, with complete grants or explicit blocked code views. Live discovery also found PREMIERE AI Toolbox material, but no new full grant/implemented creative-tool screen was completed for it.

Both existing project root overviews were readable. Current full-file/license requests returned HTTP200 bot challenges; they are recorded as unavailable evidence and no challenge was bypassed. No new eligible source was cleared.

Current diffuser README, full MIT grant, Cargo manifest and inference source were inspected. Its author-local absolute dependency path prevents a portable unchanged checkout; no unrelated new project was cleared from this bounded source review.

PyPI game-localizer/gameloc JSON and TensorStack NuGet metadata were inspected. Manimvox and Brandly HTML returned challenges rather than usable package documentation; package metadata alone never clears software/model rights or usability.

Interstice primary documentation and current Blender, ComfyUI, PhotoCraft, notation, subtitle, game and lighting integrations were inspected. A connector-only repository without implemented software was held; proprietary hosts and paid services remain separate.

All 94observed fields received a live primary web-source attempt beyond GitHub:100 unique URLs,99 HTTP 200 responses and oneTLSfailure;3 PDF captures were bounded at2MB. Challenge/login pages, placeholders and thin JavaScript shells were not treated as usable source evidence or quality approval.

Primary papers/project pages covered motion, brain/music mappings, relighting, codecs, acoustic/haptic fields, tactile graphics, robotic calligraphy and other adjacent practices. Complete code grants are a separate admission gate; paper provenance and owner metrics do not grant quality labels.

Current primary multilingual projects include Japanese EEG/notation workflows, Chinese CAD/manga pipelines, Arabic game subtitles, Vietnamese translation, Portuguese accessibility, Korean game tooling and bilingual publication. Language/region never substitutes for license, creative AI use or quality evidence.
